**Finding: compliant (at the fallback) — no redline proposed.**

The document does contain a minimum purchase commitment on us, but it comes with an adequate exit, so it lands within the playbook's acceptable range:

- **§ 5(a) (p0045)** obliges us to pay "not less than $____ per month" for Hosting Services and Support Services — a true minimum on the Client side, not a Vendor-side commitment.
- **§ 13 (p0078)** caps exposure at a single one-year term with automatic one-year renewals, defeasible by thirty days' notice of intent not to renew. No multi-year lock-in, so we are clear of walk-away territory.
- **§ 14 (p0079)** is the decisive provision: we may elect to terminate by written notice, with services (and therefore the minimums) running only to the last day of the month following the notice month — effectively a ~30-day exit.
- There is **no shortfall payment, make-whole, liquidated damages or penalty**, and no volume cap on our usage. We pay the monthly minimum only for months the Agreement is live, which is a true-up in substance.

Two items flagged in the rationale as commercial notes rather than deviations:

1. The minimum figures are left **blank ($____)** and should be filled at or below our expected run-rate before signature — the clause is only benign if the numbers are.
2. **§ 6 (p0047)** carves the minimum monthly fees out of our documentation and charge-dispute rights. The cross-reference to "Section 4" appears to be a mis-numbering of the Compensation section (the section is captioned 5 but internally referenced as 4) — worth correcting, and it may be picked up by an audit/dispute-rights rule, but it does not defeat the fallback on MINCOMMIT.
